answers.brief_reasoning: MR = 100 - 4Q. Setting MR = MC gives 100 - 4Q = 20, so Q = 20. Price from demand: P = 100 - 2(20) = 60. Demand meets the price axis at 100 and the quantity axis at 50. MR meets the price axis at 100 and the quantity axis at 25. MC and ATC are the same horizontal line at 20.
answers.final_answer: Qm = 20, Pm = $60. Demand intercepts: P = 100, Q = 50. MR intercepts: P = 100, Q = 25. MC = ATC is a horizontal line at $20.

answers.brief_reasoning: Profit = (P - ATC) × Q = (60 - 20) × 20 = 800. Shade the rectangle between $20 and $60 from Q = 0 to Q = 20.
Under perfect competition, P = MC = 20, so Q = 40. DWL = 0.5 × (40 - 20) × (60 - 20) = 400. Shade the triangle between demand and MC from Q = 20 to Q = 40.

At a price of $40, buyers demand Q = 30. Up to Q = 30, MR stays flat at $40 because the firm can't raise its price above the ceiling. Since $40 is greater than MC of $20, every unit up to 30 adds to profit. After Q = 30, the firm moves back onto the original MR curve, which is below MC (100 - 4(30) = -20). So the firm produces 30. Profit = (40 - 20) × 30 = 600.
answers.final_answer: Q = 30 and profit = $600. Quantity rises because the ceiling makes MR equal to $40 up to 30 units, and that is above MC. The firm no longer has to cut its price to sell more units.
